title: Zaheer Khan Becomes Co-Owner of LPL's Jaffna Kings After Anchor Sports Takeover
excerpt: Stockholm-based Anchor Sports AB completes acquisition of the four-time LPL champions after previous owners were ousted mid-tournament over match-fixing allegations and financial failures.
body:
• Stockholm-based Anchor Sports AB has acquired the Jaffna Kings franchise, with former India fast bowler Zaheer Khan joining as co-owner alongside Anchor Sports owner Nagendra Siddoutam.
  • The franchise has been rebranded as Anchor Jaffna Kings, adding to Anchor Sports' global portfolio that includes teams in Belgium and Canada.
  • Previous owners Sports Commune had their franchise agreement terminated after co-owner Manjot Kalra was arrested for alleged match-fixing on the tournament's opening day.
  • Jaffna Kings remain the LPL's most successful franchise with four titles in five seasons and currently sit in the top two of this season's standings.

New Ownership Takes Shape

Former India fast-bowling great Zaheer Khan has entered the ownership ranks of the Lanka Premier League after Stockholm-based Anchor Sports AB completed the acquisition of the four-time champions Jaffna Kings, according to IANS.

https://x.com/NewsWireLK/status/2084721128149586091

The franchise will be rebranded as Anchor Jaffna Kings under the new ownership structure, with Zaheer joining Anchor Sports owner Nagendra Siddoutam as co-owner. The acquisition marks a swift resolution to weeks of turmoil that engulfed the franchise after its previous ownership group collapsed mid-season.

"I've always admired the calibre, innovation and variety of bowling talent that comes out of Sri Lanka; it's a country I've visited, competed in, and hold very fond memories of. To now be part of Sri Lankan cricket as an owner is something I'm genuinely thrilled about."

— Zaheer Khan, Co-owner, Anchor Jaffna Kings

From Scandal to Stability

The takeover comes after one of the most dramatic ownership crises in franchise T20 cricket. Sports Commune, the group led by former India Under-19 batter Manjot Kalra and entrepreneur Mayank Goel, had acquired the Jaffna Kings ahead of LPL Season 6 in May 2026.

On July 17 — the tournament's opening day — Kalra was arrested by Sri Lanka's Special Investigations Unit for the Prevention of Offences Relating to Sports over an alleged attempt to bribe a player with LKR 9.5 million (approximately $30,000). A player had flagged the approach ten days earlier, according to Cricbuzz.

With one owner in custody and the other absent, the financial chain broke. Players went unpaid, and during a July 22 match against Colombo Kaps, the Jaffna Kings squad taped over sponsor logos on their kits in a visible protest. Sri Lanka Cricket and IPG, the tournament's rights holder, terminated Sports Commune's franchise agreement on July 23-24 and assumed direct operational control.

Anchor Sports' Global Cricket Ambitions

The Jaffna Kings acquisition extends Anchor Sports AB's growing footprint in international franchise cricket. The group already owns the Antwerp Anchors in the European T20 Premier League — where Zaheer also serves as co-owner alongside marquee player Andre Russell — and the Vancouver Anchors men's and women's teams in Canada's Super 60 League.

Nagendra Siddoutam, owner of Anchor Sports, framed the deal as part of a broader strategy. "Sri Lanka has a rich cricketing heritage, and the LPL has established itself as a well-run, highly competitive league in a short span of time," he said. "The Jaffna Anchors will be a natural extension of what we're building globally — franchises that are rooted in their local communities while being part of a connected, international Anchor network."

A Familiar Face for Indian Cricket Fans

Zaheer Khan's transition from the pitch to the boardroom continues a path he began with the Antwerp Anchors earlier in 2026. A left-arm fast bowler who claimed 311 Test wickets and 282 ODI wickets across a 15-year international career, Zaheer was a central figure in India's 2011 Cricket World Cup triumph. His involvement in LPL ownership adds significant profile to a league that has struggled with governance issues despite its competitive cricket.

The appointment also carries relevance for the Indian diaspora in Sri Lanka and the broader South Asian region, as another high-profile Indian cricketer deepens ties with Sri Lankan cricket at a time when the sport's franchise ecosystem increasingly operates across borders.

On the Field, Jaffna Still Dominant

Despite the off-field chaos, Jaffna Kings have continued to perform. Led by Sri Lankan batter Bhanuka Rajapaksa, the side has won four of six matches this season and sits in the top two on the points table. The team also features all-rounder Dunith Wellalage, who was pre-signed before the season. The LPL 2026 season, which began on July 17, is scheduled to conclude on August 8.

LPL Tournament Director Samantha Dodanwela welcomed the new ownership: "Having an owner of Zaheer Khan's calibre involved with the Anchor Jaffna Kings is a real boost for the league. The mentorship and direction he can offer our young Sri Lankan players will be enormous."
nri_angle: Former Indian cricket great Zaheer Khan deepens cross-border cricket ties by entering Sri Lankan franchise ownership, reflecting the increasingly borderless nature of South Asian cricket's franchise ecosystem.
